title: Practical Foundations for Programming Languages (2nd edition, abbreviated)
byline: Robert Harper · Cambridge University Press, 2016; abbreviated online edition with corrections, from the author’s site
note: The free online edition keeps all 18 parts but only 17 of the printed book’s chapters; omitted parts appear here as single entries that point to the corresponding chapters in the 2012 pre-publication draft, which is also in your Drive (harper.pdf). The appendices are not broken down. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: Harper’s framework for defining and analyzing programming languages with type theory: every feature is given a statics (typing judgments) and a dynamics (transition rules), and type safety is proved as progress plus preservation. The book builds from abstract binding trees and inductive definitions through total and partial functional languages (System T, PCF), finite and infinite data types, polymorphism (System F) and abstract types, dynamic typing as a special case of static typing, subtyping and dynamic dispatch, control (stacks, exceptions, continuations), symbols, mutable state (Modernized Algol, references), parallelism and cost semantics, concurrency (process calculus, Concurrent Algol), modules, and equational reasoning and parametricity. The abbreviated online edition includes the core chapters of each of these threads.
